type inPC struct {
	I int

// Code generated by vandorf. DO NOT EDIT.

package app

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"example.com/app/types"
)

type envP struct {
	inPA inPA
	outPA int
	inPId1 inPId1
	outPId1 types.POut
	inPB inPB
	outPB []int
	inPId2 inPId2
	outPId2 types.POut
	inPId3 inPId3
	outPId3 types.POut
	inPC inPC
	outPC int
}

const (
	pcP_PA = iota
	pcP_PId1
	pcP_PB
	pcP_PId2
	pcP_PId3
	pcP_PC
)

// RunP runs proc P.
func RunP(ctx context.Context) (types.POut, error) {
	var zero types.POut
	env := &envP{}
	env.inPA = inPA{}
	pc := pcP_PA
	for {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return zero, err
		}
		switch pc {
		case pcP_PA:
			this, err := unimplementedPA(ctx)
			if err != nil {
				return zero, fmt.Errorf("P.A: %w", err)
			}
			zeroOut(&env.inPA)
			_ = this
			{
				if (this > 0) {
					env.inPId1 = inPId1{Value: types.POut{N: this, Tags: []string{"pos"}}}
					pc = pcP_PId1
					continue
				}
			}
			{
				if (this == 0) {
					env.inPB = inPB{I: this}
					pc = pcP_PB
					continue
				}
			}
			env.inPId2 = inPId2{Value: types.POut{N: (-this), Tags: []string{}}}
			pc = pcP_PId2
			continue
		case pcP_PId1:
			this := env.inPId1.Value
			zeroOut(&env.inPId1)
			_ = this
			return this, nil
		case pcP_PB:
			this, err := unimplementedPB(ctx, env.inPB.I)
			if err != nil {
				return zero, fmt.Errorf("P.B: %w", err)
			}
			zeroOut(&env.inPB)
			_ = this
			results, err := fanOut(ctx, this, func(ctx context.Context, elem int) (int, error) {
				env := *env
				return runPRegion1(ctx, &env, elem)
			})
			if err != nil {
				return zero, err
			}
			{
				this := results
				_ = this
				env.inPId3 = inPId3{Value: types.POut{N: len(this), Tags: []string{"many"}}}
				pc = pcP_PId3
				continue
			}
		case pcP_PId2:
			this := env.inPId2.Value
			zeroOut(&env.inPId2)
			_ = this
			return this, nil
		case pcP_PId3:
			this := env.inPId3.Value
			zeroOut(&env.inPId3)
			_ = this
			return this, nil
		default:
			return zero, fmt.Errorf("P: invalid state %d", pc)
		}
	}
}

// runPRegion1 runs one element of the for each from P.B.
func runPRegion1(ctx context.Context, env *envP, elem int) (int, error) {
	var zero int
	this := elem
	_ = this
	env.inPC = inPC{I: this}
	pc := pcP_PC
	for {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return zero, err
		}
		switch pc {
		case pcP_PC:
			this, err := unimplementedPC(ctx, env.inPC.I)
			if err != nil {
				return zero, fmt.Errorf("P.C: %w", err)
			}
			zeroOut(&env.inPC)
			_ = this
			return this, nil
		default:
			return zero, fmt.Errorf("P: invalid state %d", pc)
		}
	}
}


==== /runtime_vandorf.go
// Code generated by vandorf. DO NOT EDIT.

package app

import (
	"cmp"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"runtime"
	"slices"
	"sync"
	"unsafe"
)

// mapGet looks up k, failing if it's missing.
func mapGet[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, k K) (V, error) {
	v, ok := m[k]
	if !ok {
		return v, fmt.Errorf("key %v not found", k)
	}
	return v, nil
}

// sliceGet indexes xs, failing if i is out of range.
func sliceGet[E any](xs []E, i int) (E, error) {
	if i < 0 || i >= len(xs) {
		var zero E
		return zero, fmt.Errorf("index %d out of range [0, %d)", i, len(xs))
	}
	return xs[i], nil
}

func mapHas[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, k K) bool {
	_, ok := m[k]
	return ok
}

// mapKeys returns m's keys in order.
func mapKeys[K cmp.Ordered, V any](m map[K]V) []K {
	ks := make([]K, 0, len(m))
	for k := range m {
		ks = append(ks, k)
	}
	slices.Sort(ks)
	return ks
}

// mapValues returns m's values in key order.
func mapValues[K cmp.Ordered, V any](m map[K]V) []V {
	vs := make([]V, 0, len(m))
	for _, k := range mapKeys(m) {
		vs = append(vs, m[k])
	}
	return vs
}

// mapMerge returns a new map with a's entries and b's, b winning. Maps
// are values in vandorf, so the arguments are never changed.
func mapMerge[K comparable, V any](a, b map[K]V) map[K]V {
	r := make(map[K]V, len(a)+len(b))
	for k, v := range a {
		r[k] = v
	}
	for k, v := range b {
		r[k] = v
	}
	return r
}

// Arrays that sliceConcat builds keep spare capacity in reserve. The
// reserve is hidden from every slice handed out, whose capacity is clipped
// to its length, so code that appends to one (implementations included)
// always copies. reserves records each such array by the address of its
// first element: how much of it is filled. A + whose left side ends
// exactly there appends into the reserve; any other copies. So values
// never change where anyone can see, and a loop like acc + [x] costs
// amortized O(1) per element. A finalizer drops an array's entry when it's
// freed, before its address can be reused.
type reserve struct{ filled, cap int }

var (
	reservesMu sync.Mutex
	reserves   = map[uintptr]reserve{}
)

// sliceConcat returns a new slice with a's elements, then b's; neither
// changes.
func sliceConcat[E any](a, b []E) []E {
	n := len(a) + len(b)
	var zero E
	size := int(unsafe.Sizeof(zero))
	if size == 0 {
		// All zero-size arrays share one address: nothing to reserve.
		return make([]E, n)
	}
	if p := unsafe.SliceData(a); p != nil {
		base := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(p))
		reservesMu.Lock()
		if r, ok := reserves[base]; ok && r.filled == len(a) && n <= r.cap {
			reserves[base] = reserve{n, r.cap}
			reservesMu.Unlock()
			full := unsafe.Slice(p, r.cap)
			copy(full[len(a):n], b)
			return full[:n:n]
		}
		reservesMu.Unlock()
	}
	// Room to double, and over 16 bytes: the tiny allocator's blocks may
	// never be finalized.
	c := max(2*n, 16/size+1)
	r := make([]E, n, c)
	copy(r, a)
	copy(r[len(a):], b)
	p := unsafe.SliceData(r)
	base := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(p))
	reservesMu.Lock()
	reserves[base] = reserve{n, c}
	reservesMu.Unlock()
	runtime.SetFinalizer(p, func(*E) {
		reservesMu.Lock()
		delete(reserves, base)
		reservesMu.Unlock()
	})
	return r[:n:n]
}

// mapRemove returns a new map without the keys ks.
func mapRemove[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, ks []K) map[K]V {
	r := make(map[K]V, len(m))
	for k, v := range m {
		r[k] = v
	}
	for _, k := range ks {
		delete(r, k)
	}
	return r
}

// ptrTo boxes a value, for fields that would otherwise make a type contain
// itself.
func ptrTo[T any](v T) *T {
	return &v
}

// zeroOut clears a slot no later state reads, so the garbage collector can
// reclaim what it held.
func zeroOut[T any](p *T) {
	var zero T
	*p = zero
}

// joinAll runs fs concurrently and waits for all of them: a spawn's joined
// branches. The first error cancels the rest and is returned.
func joinAll(ctx context.Context, fs ...func(context.Context) error) error {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	defer cancel()
	var (
		wg    sync.WaitGroup
		once  sync.Once
		first error
	)
	for _, f := range fs {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			if err := f(ctx); err != nil {
				once.Do(func() { first = err; cancel() })
			}
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	return first
}

// spawnDetached runs f on a goroutine of its own, a spawn's detached branch:
// nothing waits for it, it outlives ctx's cancellation, and a failure is
// only reported.
func spawnDetached(ctx context.Context, f func(context.Context) error) {
	ctx = context.WithoutCancel(ctx)
	go func() {
		if err := f(ctx); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "error: %v\n", err)
		}
	}()
}

// fanOut runs f over xs concurrently and returns the results in input order.
// The first error cancels the remaining elements.
func fanOut[E, R any](ctx context.Context, xs []E, f func(context.Context, E) (R, error)) ([]R, error) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	defer cancel()
	out := make([]R, len(xs))
	var (
		wg    sync.WaitGroup
		once  sync.Once
		first error
	)
	for i, x := range xs {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			r, err := f(ctx, x)
			if err != nil {
				once.Do(func() { first = err; cancel() })
				return
			}
			out[i] = r
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	return out, first
}

package app

// unimplementedPA stands in for P.A, which names no .go implementation. Write
//	func Name(ctx context.Context) (int, error)
// and add `= "file.go:Name"` to its declaration.
func unimplementedPA(ctx context.Context) (int, error) {
	var zero int
	return zero, errors.New("P.A is not implemented")
}

// unimplementedPB stands in for P.B, which names no .go implementation. Write
//	func Name(ctx context.Context, i int) ([]int, error)
// and add `= "file.go:Name"` to its declaration.
func unimplementedPB(ctx context.Context, _ int) ([]int, error) {
	var zero []int
	return zero, errors.New("P.B is not implemented")
}

// unimplementedPC stands in for P.C, which names no .go implementation. Write
//	func Name(ctx context.Context, i int) (int, error)
// and add `= "file.go:Name"` to its declaration.
func unimplementedPC(ctx context.Context, _ int) (int, error) {
	var zero int
	return zero, errors.New("P.C is not implemented")
}

}

// unimplementedPC stands in for P.C, which names no .go implementation. Write
//	func Name(ctx context.Context, i int) (int, error)
// and add `= "file.go:Name"` to its declaration.
func unimplementedPC(ctx context.Context, _ int) (int, error) {
	var zero int
	return zero, errors.New("P.C is not implemented")
}

package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"example.com/app/types"
)

type envP struct {
	inPA inPA
	outPA int
	inPId1 inPId1
	outPId1 types.POut
	inPB inPB
	outPB []int
	inPId2 inPId2
	outPId2 types.POut
	inPId3 inPId3
	outPId3 types.POut
	inPC inPC
	outPC int
}

const (
	pcP_PA = iota
	pcP_PId1
	pcP_PB
	pcP_PId2
	pcP_PId3
	pcP_PC
)

// RunP runs proc P.
func RunP(ctx context.Context) (types.POut, error) {
	var zero types.POut
	env := &envP{}
	env.inPA = inPA{}
	pc := pcP_PA
	for {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return zero, err
		}
		switch pc {
		case pcP_PA:
			this, err := unimplementedPA(ctx)
			if err != nil {
				return zero, fmt.Errorf("P.A: %w", err)
			}
			zeroOut(&env.inPA)
			_ = this
			{
				if (this > 0) {
					env.inPId1 = inPId1{Value: types.POut{N: this, Tags: []string{"pos"}}}
					pc = pcP_PId1
					continue
				}
			}
			{
				if (this == 0) {
					env.inPB = inPB{I: this}
					pc = pcP_PB
					continue
				}
			}
			env.inPId2 = inPId2{Value: types.POut{N: (-this), Tags: []string{}}}
			pc = pcP_PId2
			continue
		case pcP_PId1:
			this := env.inPId1.Value
			zeroOut(&env.inPId1)
			_ = this
			return this, nil
		case pcP_PB:
			this, err := unimplementedPB(ctx, env.inPB.I)
			if err != nil {
				return zero, fmt.Errorf("P.B: %w", err)
			}
			zeroOut(&env.inPB)
			_ = this
			results, err := fanOut(ctx, this, func(ctx context.Context, elem int) (int, error) {
				env := *env
				return runPRegion1(ctx, &env, elem)
			})
			if err != nil {
				return zero, err
			}
			{
				this := results
				_ = this
				env.inPId3 = inPId3{Value: types.POut{N: len(this), Tags: []string{"many"}}}
				pc = pcP_PId3
				continue
			}
		case pcP_PId2:
			this := env.inPId2.Value
			zeroOut(&env.inPId2)
			_ = this
			return this, nil
		case pcP_PId3:
			this := env.inPId3.Value
			zeroOut(&env.inPId3)
			_ = this
			return this, nil
		default:
			return zero, fmt.Errorf("P: invalid state %d", pc)
		}
	}
}

// runPRegion1 runs one element of the for each from P.B.
func runPRegion1(ctx context.Context, env *envP, elem int) (int, error) {
	var zero int
	this := elem
	_ = this
	env.inPC = inPC{I: this}
	pc := pcP_PC
	for {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return zero, err
		}
		switch pc {
		case pcP_PC:
			this, err := unimplementedPC(ctx, env.inPC.I)
			if err != nil {
				return zero, fmt.Errorf("P.C: %w", err)
			}
			zeroOut(&env.inPC)
			_ = this
			return this, nil
		default:
			return zero, fmt.Errorf("P: invalid state %d", pc)
		}
	}
}


==== /runtime_vandorf.go
// Code generated by vandorf. DO NOT EDIT.

package main

import (
	"cmp"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"runtime"
	"slices"
	"sync"
	"unsafe"
)

// mapGet looks up k, failing if it's missing.
func mapGet[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, k K) (V, error) {
	v, ok := m[k]
	if !ok {
		return v, fmt.Errorf("key %v not found", k)
	}
	return v, nil
}

// sliceGet indexes xs, failing if i is out of range.
func sliceGet[E any](xs []E, i int) (E, error) {
	if i < 0 || i >= len(xs) {
		var zero E
		return zero, fmt.Errorf("index %d out of range [0, %d)", i, len(xs))
	}
	return xs[i], nil
}

func mapHas[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, k K) bool {
	_, ok := m[k]
	return ok
}

// mapKeys returns m's keys in order.
func mapKeys[K cmp.Ordered, V any](m map[K]V) []K {
	ks := make([]K, 0, len(m))
	for k := range m {
		ks = append(ks, k)
	}
	slices.Sort(ks)
	return ks
}

// mapValues returns m's values in key order.
func mapValues[K cmp.Ordered, V any](m map[K]V) []V {
	vs := make([]V, 0, len(m))
	for _, k := range mapKeys(m) {
		vs = append(vs, m[k])
	}
	return vs
}

// mapMerge returns a new map with a's entries and b's, b winning. Maps
// are values in vandorf, so the arguments are never changed.
func mapMerge[K comparable, V any](a, b map[K]V) map[K]V {
	r := make(map[K]V, len(a)+len(b))
	for k, v := range a {
		r[k] = v
	}
	for k, v := range b {
		r[k] = v
	}
	return r
}

// Arrays that sliceConcat builds keep spare capacity in reserve. The
// reserve is hidden from every slice handed out, whose capacity is clipped
// to its length, so code that appends to one (implementations included)
// always copies. reserves records each such array by the address of its
// first element: how much of it is filled. A + whose left side ends
// exactly there appends into the reserve; any other copies. So values
// never change where anyone can see, and a loop like acc + [x] costs
// amortized O(1) per element. A finalizer drops an array's entry when it's
// freed, before its address can be reused.
type reserve struct{ filled, cap int }

var (
	reservesMu sync.Mutex
	reserves   = map[uintptr]reserve{}
)

// sliceConcat returns a new slice with a's elements, then b's; neither
// changes.
func sliceConcat[E any](a, b []E) []E {
	n := len(a) + len(b)
	var zero E
	size := int(unsafe.Sizeof(zero))
	if size == 0 {
		// All zero-size arrays share one address: nothing to reserve.
		return make([]E, n)
	}
	if p := unsafe.SliceData(a); p != nil {
		base := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(p))
		reservesMu.Lock()
		if r, ok := reserves[base]; ok && r.filled == len(a) && n <= r.cap {
			reserves[base] = reserve{n, r.cap}
			reservesMu.Unlock()
			full := unsafe.Slice(p, r.cap)
			copy(full[len(a):n], b)
			return full[:n:n]
		}
		reservesMu.Unlock()
	}
	// Room to double, and over 16 bytes: the tiny allocator's blocks may
	// never be finalized.
	c := max(2*n, 16/size+1)
	r := make([]E, n, c)
	copy(r, a)
	copy(r[len(a):], b)
	p := unsafe.SliceData(r)
	base := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(p))
	reservesMu.Lock()
	reserves[base] = reserve{n, c}
	reservesMu.Unlock()
	runtime.SetFinalizer(p, func(*E) {
		reservesMu.Lock()
		delete(reserves, base)
		reservesMu.Unlock()
	})
	return r[:n:n]
}

// mapRemove returns a new map without the keys ks.
func mapRemove[K comparable, V any](m map[K]V, ks []K) map[K]V {
	r := make(map[K]V, len(m))
	for k, v := range m {
		r[k] = v
	}
	for _, k := range ks {
		delete(r, k)
	}
	return r
}

// ptrTo boxes a value, for fields that would otherwise make a type contain
// itself.
func ptrTo[T any](v T) *T {
	return &v
}

// zeroOut clears a slot no later state reads, so the garbage collector can
// reclaim what it held.
func zeroOut[T any](p *T) {
	var zero T
	*p = zero
}

// joinAll runs fs concurrently and waits for all of them: a spawn's joined
// branches. The first error cancels the rest and is returned.
func joinAll(ctx context.Context, fs ...func(context.Context) error) error {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	defer cancel()
	var (
		wg    sync.WaitGroup
		once  sync.Once
		first error
	)
	for _, f := range fs {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			if err := f(ctx); err != nil {
				once.Do(func() { first = err; cancel() })
			}
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	return first
}

// spawnDetached runs f on a goroutine of its own, a spawn's detached branch:
// nothing waits for it, it outlives ctx's cancellation, and a failure is
// only reported.
func spawnDetached(ctx context.Context, f func(context.Context) error) {
	ctx = context.WithoutCancel(ctx)
	go func() {
		if err := f(ctx); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "error: %v\n", err)
		}
	}()
}

// fanOut runs f over xs concurrently and returns the results in input order.
// The first error cancels the remaining elements.
func fanOut[E, R any](ctx context.Context, xs []E, f func(context.Context, E) (R, error)) ([]R, error) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	defer cancel()
	out := make([]R, len(xs))
	var (
		wg    sync.WaitGroup
		once  sync.Once
		first error
	)
	for i, x := range xs {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			r, err := f(ctx, x)
			if err != nil {
				once.Do(func() { first = err; cancel() })
				return
			}
			out[i] = r
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	return out, first
}

==== ../cmd/bin/main_vandorf.go
// Code generated by vandorf. DO NOT EDIT.

// Command bin runs proc P, taking its parameters as arguments.
//
//	usage: bin
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	procs "example.com/app"
)

const usage = "usage: bin"

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) != 1 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, usage)
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	result, err := procs.RunP(context.Background())
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "error:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Printf("%+v\n", result)
}
